In the mathematical field of [[differential geometry]], the '''Kulkarni–Nomizu product''' (named for [[Ravindra Shripad Kulkarni]] and [[Katsumi Nomizu]]) is defined for two {{nowrap|(0, 2)}}-[[tensor]]s and gives as a result a {{nowrap|(0, 4)}}-tensor.

==Definition==
If ''h'' and ''k'' are symmetric {{nowrap|(0, 2)}}-tensors, then the product is defined via:<ref>Some authors include an overall factor {{sfrac|1|2}} in the definition.</ref>

:<math>\begin{align}
  (h {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} k)(X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4) :={}
        &h(X_1, X_3)k(X_2, X_4) + h(X_2, X_4)k(X_1, X_3) \\
        &{}- h(X_1, X_4)k(X_2, X_3) - h(X_2, X_3)k(X_1, X_4) \\[3pt]
  {}={} &\begin{vmatrix}
           h(X_1, X_3) &h (X_1, X_4)\\
           k(X_2, X_3) &k (X_2, X_4)
         \end{vmatrix} + \begin{vmatrix}
           k(X_1, X_3) &k (X_1, X_4)\\
           h(X_2, X_3) &h (X_2, X_4)
         \end{vmatrix}
\end{align}</math>
where the ''X''<sub>''j''</sub> are tangent vectors and <math>|\cdot|</math> is the [[matrix determinant]]. Note that <math>h {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} k = k {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} h</math>, as it is clear from the second expression.  

With respect to a basis <math>\{\partial_i\}</math> of the [[tangent space]], it takes the compact form
:<math>(h~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~k)_{ijlm}
  = (h{~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~}k )(\partial_i, \partial_j, \partial_l,\partial_m)
  = 2h_{i [l}k_{m]j} + 2h_{j [m}k_{l]i}\,,
</math>
where <math>[\dots]</math> denotes the [[Antisymmetric tensor#Notation|total antisymmetrisation symbol]].

The Kulkarni–Nomizu product is a special case of the product in the graded algebra
:<math>\bigoplus_{p=1}^n S^2\left(\Omega^p M\right),</math>

where, on simple elements,
:<math>(\alpha\cdot\beta) {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} (\gamma\cdot\delta) = (\alpha\wedge\gamma)\odot(\beta\wedge\delta)</math>

(<math>\odot</math> denotes the [[Symmetric tensor#Symmetric product|symmetric product]]).

==Properties==
The Kulkarni–Nomizu product of a pair of symmetric tensors has the algebraic symmetries of the [[Riemann tensor]].<ref>A {{nowrap|(0, 4)}}-tensor that satisfies the skew-symmetry property, the interchange symmetry property and the first (algebraic) Bianchi identity (see [[Riemann curvature tensor#symmetries and identities|symmetries and identities of the Riemann curvature]]) is called an '''algebraic curvature tensor'''.</ref> For instance, on [[space form]]s (i.e. spaces of constant [[sectional curvature]]) and two-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifolds, the [[Riemann curvature tensor]] has a simple expression in terms of the Kulkarni–Nomizu product of the [[Metric tensor|metric]] <math>g=g_{ij}dx^i\otimes dx^j</math> with itself; namely, if we denote by

:<math>\operatorname{R}(\partial_i, \partial_j) \partial_k = {R^l}_{ijk} \partial_l</math>
the {{nowrap|(1, 3)}}-curvature tensor and by
:<math>\operatorname{Rm}=R_{ijkl} dx^i\otimes dx^j\otimes dx^k\otimes dx^l</math>
the Riemann curvature tensor with <math>R_{ijkl}= g_{im} {R^m}_{jkl}</math>, then

:<math>\operatorname{Rm}=\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{4} g~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~g,</math>

where <math>\operatorname{Scal}=\operatorname{tr}_g\operatorname{Ric}={R^i}_i</math> is the [[scalar curvature]] and
:<math>\operatorname{Ric}(Y,Z) = 
  \operatorname{tr}_g\lbrace X\mapsto\operatorname{R}(X,Y)Z\rbrace</math>

is the [[Ricci tensor]], which in components reads <math>R_{ij}={R^k}_{ikj}</math>.
Expanding the Kulkarni–Nomizu product <math>g~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~g</math> using the definition from above, one obtains

:<math>R_{ijkl}
  = \frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{4} g_{i[k} g_{l]j}
  = \frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{2} ( g_{ik} g_{jl} - g_{il} g_{jk} )\,.
</math>

This is the same expression as stated in the article on the [[Riemann curvature tensor]].

For this very reason, it is commonly used to express the contribution that the [[Ricci curvature]] (or rather, the [[Schouten tensor]]) and the [[Weyl tensor]] each makes to the [[curvature of Riemannian manifolds|curvature]] of a [[Riemannian manifold]].  This so-called [[Ricci decomposition]] is useful in [[differential geometry]].

When there is a [[metric tensor]] ''g'', the Kulkarni–Nomizu product of ''g'' with itself is the identity endomorphism of the space of 2-forms, Ω<sup>2</sup>(''M''), under the identification (using the metric) of the [[endomorphism ring]] End(Ω<sup>2</sup>(''M'')) with the tensor product Ω<sup>2</sup>(''M'')&nbsp;⊗&nbsp;Ω<sup>2</sup>(''M'').

A Riemannian manifold has constant [[sectional curvature]] ''k'' [[if and only if]] the Riemann tensor has the form
:<math>R = \frac{k}{2}g {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} g</math>
where ''g'' is the [[metric tensor]].
